taxonomy.label: A
taxonomy.explanation: The bound source assumes Hausdorff (T2Space), whereas the formal root assumes only R1Space. The latter admits non-Hausdorff spaces, including the two-point indiscrete space. This is an applicability generalization, not a refutation of the formal theorem.

semantic_argument: Mathlib LocallyCompactSpace.local_compact_nhds requires a compact neighbourhood inside every neighbourhood. WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace requires one compact neighbourhood at every point. These match the two source predicates; IsCompact has the finite-subcover characterization without a Hausdorff requirement.
The explicit root contains only TopologicalSpace and R1Space assumptions, with no T0Space, T1Space or T2Space. Neither compactness class supplies such a separation assumption.
Mathlib T2Space.r1Space proves Hausdorff implies R1. Mathlib also derives T2 from R1 plus T0, but the root does not require T0.

For X={0,1} with open sets exactly empty and X, all points have identical neighbourhoods, so R1 holds. Distinct points cannot have disjoint neighbourhoods, so Hausdorff fails. The whole finite space is compact and is the sole neighbourhood of each point, so both local compactness properties hold. This distinguishes the premise domains, not the truth values of the two theorems.

The source file explicitly describes the result as generalized to R1Space. The reverse implication uses the existing Mathlib WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace.locallyCompactSpace instance under R1; this is not an unbound predicate or a missing data definition.

Specializing the formal theorem to T2Space recovers the source assertion. Under a separate policy accepting correct generalizations this could be considered aligned, but no such exception is assumed over the current repository applicability criterion.
